rows.evidence: Q1: Application section and Results <U+2014> authors run their own daily 1992<U+2013>2006 MOBIDIC-WRM simulation of the Arno basin at 200 m resolution, calibrated on 15 sub-basins (1993<U+2013>1998) and compared with measured flow duration curves at gauging stations (Fig. 2, Fig. 3). Q2: Application section <U+2014> land cover, geology and soil hydraulic properties retrieved from existing maps and remote sensing data; Water budget section and Fig. 5/Table 2 <U+2014> residual flow WB = Q <U+2212> EF <U+2212> W computed per reach, number of summer days below environmental flow used to classify 44 sections/sub-basins into four deficit classes, critical areas mapped (Chiana, Ambra, Greve, Pesa, Egola, Era, upper Ombrone, Bisenzio), and different critical levels correspond to government requirements such as constraints on new withdrawal permissions in the Water Budget Management Plan; model output compared with measured discharge (Fig. 2, Fig. 3). Q4: Eq. 13<U+2013>14 and Table 2 <U+2014> the tool explicitly models the intermediate quantities (natural discharge, withdrawals, wastewater returns, Q7,2 environmental flow, residual flow and days below EF) through which critical areas are identified. Q6: Application and Water budget sections <U+2014> results reported at the scale of the whole Arno basin (~8000 km2), 15 sub-basins and 44 river sections, used as basis for the basin Water Management Plan. Q8: Results <U+2014> poor agreement at stations where groundwater dynamics need more detailed representation than the lumped approach; groundwater modelled in simplified linear-reservoir form because of scarce aquifer data; peaks and low base flows estimated with varying accuracy (Fig. 3).
rows.notes: Remote sensing is only one input (land cover, soil properties from RS data); the tool is a distributed hydrological model and calibration here used gauged discharge, not the remotely-sensed LST capability mentioned in the abstract. Q2 answered yes because the study reports its own basin-scale identification of critical sub-areas and their link to withdrawal restrictions, but the review's attribution of this to 'remote sensing' overstates the RS role. The review context's claim of EO-derived precipitation is not supported: meteorological data came from the regional ground network. Q3 no: critical-area results rest on the model alone, validated only against gauge flow duration curves, with no independent method (e.g., observed drought impacts). Q5 no: single basin/climate, sub-basins are not distinct regions. Q7 no: data-availability remarks are limitations, not stated requirements for the effect. Q9 no: no dispersion or uncertainty measures reported.
